served.stem: Early spontaneous abortion is most often associated with which kind of genetic abnormality?
choices: Triploidy, from two sperm fertilizing one egg
served.bankWhy: Most early pregnancy losses with an identified genetic cause are chromosomal, and among those the autosomal trisomies are the largest group. Think about why: an extra whole chromosome unbalances the dosage of hundreds of genes at once, which is far more disruptive than a single base change. When a stem asks what is most often behind early loss, reach for whole chromosome errors first.

choiceTexts: Triploidy, from two sperm fertilizing one egg

answer.line: Think scale. A whole extra chromosome throws off hundreds of genes at once. Autosomal trisomies are the largest cause of early loss.

steps: Ask what error is big enough to stop development early. One base or one flipped piece rarely is; a whole extra chromosome is.
Among early losses with a chromosome error, autosomal trisomies are the largest group, well ahead of triploidy and structural changes.
Trisomies come from nondisjunction in meiosis: a pair fails to separate, so one gamete carries an extra copy.

choices.note: An unbalanced translocation can end a pregnancy, often passed down from a balanced carrier parent. It accounts for far fewer losses than trisomies.
One base change usually affects one protein. That is rarely enough on its own to stop development.
An inversion flips a piece in place and keeps every gene, so carriers are often unaffected.

choices.text: Triploidy, from two sperm fertilizing one egg
choices.note: Triploidy, often from two sperm entering one egg, does cause early loss. As a group, the autosomal trisomies are more common.
One whole extra chromosome, from nondisjunction: the largest single class of early loss.

items.title: Trisomy
items.note: a whole extra copy: hundreds of genes at three doses; the largest group of early losses

items.title: Triploidy
items.note: a full extra set; a real cause, but less common
items.choice: Triploidy, from two sperm fertilizing one egg

items.title: Translocation
items.note: pieces trade places; harmful when a gamete gets them unbalanced

items.title: Inversion
items.note: a piece flipped; nothing gained or lost

items.title: Point mutation
items.note: one base changed; usually one protein

visual.alt: Six small chromosome pictures side by side: a normal pair, a trisomy with one whole extra copy, triploidy with a full extra set, a translocation, an inversion and a point mutation. Trisomy is outlined as the answer and noted as the largest group of early losses.
visual.caption: Compare how much each change throws off. A trisomy adds a whole chromosome's worth of genes.
